title: Sample-audit corpus gold correctness before migration
description:
Measure the corpus gold error rate before committing ~750 hand adjudications to migrating it.

**Why.** 1,643 of the 1,792 annotations were authored on a single day, 2026-08-30, by agent swarms: `composer-2.5-swarm` (1,002), `grok-4.6-fill-to-200` (286), `pii-signal-backport` (253), and two `grok-4.6-data-item-fill` passes (102). Only 149 came from `corpus-curation-agent`, four days earlier. An author named *fill-to-200* describes a quota rather than an observation.

1,717 annotations carry `review_state: accepted`, but what was accepted was a labeling pass, not a correctness check. Nobody has measured whether the gold is *right*.

**What incidental sampling already turned up**, while measuring other things — not an audit, so not a rate:

- `pii:email_address` annotated on a token named `clientID`
- 308 data items keyed on source field names rather than concepts (`id`, `status`, `uuid`, `key`)
- 424 distinct prose keys across 436 data-flow annotations
- one component label set to `third_party`, a type rather than a subtype
- `actor:user` used 30 times for a subtype the taxonomy never declared

**Method.** Draw 50 annotations at random, stratified across the four layers and weighted by packet size. One reviewer checks each against the evidence at the pinned commit: is the subject present, is the concept right, is the evidence span correct, is the status right. Record the error rate per layer.

**Why it gates.** If the rate is low, KDATAP-a0e80b and KDATAP-8e7756 proceed with confidence. If it is high, the answer is not migrate-then-measure — it is to shrink the corpus to the packets that earn trust and migrate those. Hand-resolving 436 flow endpoints is the most expensive imaginable way to discover the annotations were wrong.

Half a day of one reviewer's time, against roughly 750 adjudications downstream.
